newsitem.title: JAPAN: MOF says continuous rise in surplus 'problematic'.
newsitem.headline: MOF says continuous rise in surplus 'problematic'.

text.p: Vice Finance Minister Tadashi Ogawa told reporters on Monday that a continuous rise in Japan's trade surplus as seen in the past could be "problematic" not only for Japan's economy, but also for the global economy.

Asked about the first rise in the trade surplus in 27 months, Ogawa said: "My comment is to watch it (the trade surplus) carefully for a while. An uninterrupted expansion in the trade surplus, as in the past, could be problematic for Japan's economy as well as the world economy."
He added: "The rising trade surplus shows that economic activity centring on domestic demand has become considerably firmer. It is necessary to continue such economic management.
"We can certainly expect adjustments to happen in the currency markets if the trade surplus continues to expand strongly at a rapid pace," he said.
However, Ogawa said he did not want to predict currency market directions because currencies not only reflect economic fundamentals, but also capital flows and market expectations.
The Finance Ministry announced earlier on Monday that Japan's customs-cleared trade surplus rose by 6.5 percent from a year earlier to 686.72 billion yen.
